Get or set global pipeline configuration options

Source: R/compute_graph.R
pipeline_config.Rd

Decouples project-specific parameters (study name, stage display labels, stage color palettes) from core pipeline mechanics and classes.

Usage

pipeline_config(
  study_name = NULL,
  stage_labels = NULL,
  stage_colors = NULL,
  default_formats = NULL,
  reset = FALSE,
  restore = NULL
)

Arguments

study_name

Character string for the main study title. A single `NA` clears the setting (leaving it to the session option or the default); any other value must be a single non-empty string.

stage_labels

Named character vector mapping raw stage identifiers to human-readable labels. A single `NA` clears the setting; otherwise every entry must be named and hold a single non-empty string. An empty value (`list()` or `character(0)`) means no labels.

stage_colors

Named list or character vector mapping stage identifiers to hex colors. A single `NA` clears the setting; otherwise every entry must be named and hold a single non-empty string. An empty value (`list()` or `character(0)`) means no colours.

default_formats

Optional character vector of default output formats for pipeline renderers (e.g. c("pdf", "docx")). When set, this overrides the package default across render_pipeline and create_qmd_renderer. A single `NA` clears the setting; otherwise every entry must name a known output format (or `"yaml"` / `"auto"`).

reset

Logical (default `FALSE`). When `TRUE`, clears everything set with `pipeline_config()` and falls back to the session options (or the package defaults when those are unset). It does not erase the options themselves. The reset is done first, so other arguments given in the same call are then set: `pipeline_config(study_name = "X", reset = TRUE)` leaves only the study name set.

restore

A value returned by an earlier `pipeline_config()` call: puts back exactly the package layer that call left behind (the session options are left alone). It cannot be combined with `reset` or with a value to set. This is the way to undo a call; `options(attr(cfg, "previous"))` only restores the option layer and must not be used for that, because `"previous"` holds the *effective* values (package setting over option), so restoring through `options()` would bake a package setting into a session option, where `pipeline_config(reset = TRUE)` can no longer clear it.

Value

A list containing the current configuration options, with the attributes `"previous"` and `"previous_env"`: the configuration as it was before the call (the first named the way [options()] names the session options, `pipeline.study_name` and so on; the second the raw package layer, `NULL` where nothing was set). `"previous"` holds the *effective* values, so it is for inspection (and for putting one value back with a plain `pipeline_config()` call), not for `options()`: to undo a whole call, use `pipeline_config(restore = cfg)`, which reads the `"current_env"` attribute (the package layer the returned value represents). A call with no arguments returns the current configuration.

Details

The configuration is kept in one place, inside the package, for the session: calling `pipeline_config()` with arguments changes what the pipeline functions (`create_qmd_renderer()`, `visualize_pipeline()`, `collapse_by_stage()`, `visualize_pipeline_interactive()`, `export_interactive_pipeline()`, `render_pipeline()`) read, but it does not write the session options, so a call cannot leak a changed option into later, unrelated work. The session options `pipeline.study_name`, `pipeline.stage_labels`, `pipeline.stage_colors` and `pipeline.default_formats` are only read, as a legacy default for each value that has not been set with `pipeline_config()` (set one yourself, in `.Rprofile` for example, to supply a default). This mirrors `cbe_labels()`, which likewise keeps its map in the package and only reads the `templecbe.label_map` option.
